why: The adversarial question canonicalising both sides invites: did comparing real locations weaken the check? This keeps the realpath calls and drops the parent-directory and absolute-path rejections, so any existing target is accepted. Fails exactly 2 of args.test.ts's 10: `rejects a workspace that only looks inside the checkout` (a `tmp` symlinked out of the root, which only the canonical comparison can see) and `rejects a workspace outside the checkout` (a plain sibling directory). The symlinked-root accept case and the other 7 pass under it, which is what makes the two rejection cases the guard's negative controls rather than decoration.
